```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
"Questions to be answered: What company is the most bang for buck car brand."
"What is the statistically worst electric vehicle you can buy. (Answers at the bottom)"
```

```{r}
ev_data <- read_csv("data/Electric_Vehicle_Population_Data.csv")
glimpse(ev_data)
```

```{r}
ggplot(ev_data %>% filter(`Electric Range` >= 50, `Electric Range` <= 400), aes(x = `Electric Range`)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 10, fill = "skyblue", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Histogram of Electric Range (50–400 miles)", x = "Electric Range (miles)", y = "Count")


```

```{r}
top_makes <- ev_data %>%
  count(Make, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5) %>%
  pull(Make)

box_data <- ev_data %>%
  filter(Make %in% top_makes) %>%
  drop_na(`Electric Range`)

ggplot(box_data, aes(x = Make, y = `Electric Range`, fill = Make)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Electric Range by Top 5 Makes", y = "Electric Range", x = "Make") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

```

```{r}
scatter_data <- ev_data %>%
  select(`Electric Range`, `Base MSRP`) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  filter(`Electric Range` >= 50, `Electric Range` <= 400, `Base MSRP` <= 150000)

ggplot(scatter_data, aes(x = `Electric Range`, y = `Base MSRP`)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "blue") +
  labs(title = "Electric Range vs Base MSRP ", x = "Electric Range", y = "Base MSRP")


```

```{r}
summary_stats <- ev_data %>%
  group_by(Make) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_Range = mean(`Electric Range`, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_Range = sd(`Electric Range`, na.rm = TRUE),
    Min_Range = min(`Electric Range`, na.rm = TRUE),
    Max_Range = max(`Electric Range`, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
summary_stats

```

```{r}
t_data <- ev_data %>%
  filter(Make %in% c("TESLA", "NISSAN")) %>%
  select(Make, `Electric Range`) %>%
  drop_na()

t.test(`Electric Range` ~ Make, data = t_data)

```

```{r}

anova_data <- ev_data %>%
  filter(Make %in% top_makes) %>%
  drop_na(`Electric Range`)
anova_model <- aov(`Electric Range` ~ Make, data = anova_data)
summary(anova_model)
```

```{r}
anova_data <- ev_data %>%
  filter(Make %in% top_makes) %>%
  drop_na(`Electric Range`)
```

```{r}
cor.test(scatter_data$`Electric Range`, scatter_data$`Base MSRP`)

```

```{r}
lm_model <- lm(`Base MSRP` ~ `Electric Range`, data = scatter_data)
summary(lm_model)

```

```{r}
"Answers to question: The best bang for buck car in my opinion would be a Nissan EV. The average range of it is 150 miles at an msrp of $30,000. On the other hand the statistically worst car being the chevy due to it having slightly more range at 200 miles but having a huge price hike of $50,000 for some modles."
```

```{r}
"Analysis: 
For this project, I looked at electric vehicle data to see if different car brands have different driving ranges, and if more range means a higher price. The dataset included information like the car make, electric range, and base MSRP. I made a histogram to see how electric range is spread out, and a boxplot to compare range across the top 5 most popular brands. I also made a scatterplot to check if there’s a connection between how far a car can go and how much it costs. Then I found the average, minimum, maximum, and standard deviation of electric range for each brand to summarize the data.
To see, I used a two-sample t-test to compare Tesla and Nissan, and it showed that Tesla has a much longer range on average. I also did an ANOVA test to check if different brands have different ranges, and the result told me that they did have different ranges. I ran a correlation test and a linear regression to see if range and price are connected. Both tests showed that cars with more range usually cost more. In conclusion, I found that brand does affect range, and there’s a pretty strong relationship between range and price. The more miles a car can go, the more you’re probably going to pay for it.
"
```
